source_engines: Current AP poll, verified Week 7 finals, school-confirmed Week 8 slate and reported availability. Persona arguments are editorial analysis; no odds or model probabilities.

topics.question: No. 14 Houston at No. 10 Utah: which Big 12 contender takes the next step?
topics.traditionalist: Utah is 6–0 and hosts this one. Winning another conference game would strengthen its position.
topics.analyst: Houston is 6–1 after a 35–32 win over Oklahoma State. Utah beat Colorado 27–24. Those results establish the stakes; they do not provide a win probability.
topics.evaluator: Watch how Houston’s passing game handles the road setting. There is no verified current-week injury clearance for either roster in this release.
topics.what_settles_it: Saturday October 24, 10:15 PM ET on ESPN. College GameDay airs from Utah at 9 AM–noon ET.

topics.question: Miami is No. 1 after both Georgia and Notre Dame lost. How much has the national picture changed?
topics.traditionalist: Miami is 6–0 after beating Florida State 43–35 in two overtimes. Protecting that record starts with Pittsburgh on Saturday.
topics.analyst: Eight of the 22 pregame AP-ranked teams that played lost. The October 18 AP poll moves Miami to first and BYU to second. AP ranks are not CFP committee ranks.
topics.evaluator: BYU’s 28–24 win over Notre Dame supplies a concrete result to review. The first CFP rankings are November 3.
topics.what_settles_it: Pittsburgh at Miami, Saturday noon ET on ESPN; BYU at UCF, 3:30 PM ET on FOX.

topics.question: What does Iamaleava’s season-ending injury mean for unbeaten UCLA?
topics.traditionalist: UCLA is 6–0 and ninth in the AP poll. The record still gives the Bruins a strong starting position.
topics.analyst: Chesney’s October 19 statement supersedes the earlier indefinite absence: AP/ESPN reports that knee surgery ends Iamaleava’s season.
topics.evaluator: The injury changes the quarterback context. This release does not infer practice participation or an official game-day designation for any replacement.
topics.what_settles_it: Michigan State at UCLA, Saturday 3:30 PM ET on CBS; follow official team and conference reports for further availability.

notes: Reported facts and editorial argument are distinguished. Current market lines, weather and unverified policy claims are omitted.
